5. Save

notes: Password always contains a digit (the form silently refuses one without). Employee and user deleted by teardown (deleting the employee removes the user).

scenario: Delete Employee
steps:
1. Create a new employee (via the API)
2. Search for them by last name in the Employee List
3. Click the row's delete icon
4. Confirm "Yes, Delete"
5. Navigate directly to the employee's (former) Personal Details URL
expected: "Successfully Deleted" toast appears; the employee's URL now shows "No Records Found"
notes: Only ever deletes the employee it created. Teardown then finds nothing left, which proves cleanup is safe on already-deleted data.

scenario: A Generated Employee Id Is Valid, Recognised As Ours, And Fresh
steps:
1. Generate an Employee Id
2. Check its length, whether it is recognised as a test id, and whether it is stale
expected: Exactly 10 characters (the server limit), recognised as ours, not stale
notes: No browser or network

scenario: An Id Becomes Stale Exactly At The Age Threshold, Not Before
steps:
1. Generate ids stamped just under and exactly at the stale threshold
2. Check staleness of each
expected: Just under the threshold: not stale. Exactly at it: stale.
notes: Boundary test of the purge's age rule

scenario: Ids That Are Not Ours Are Never Recognised
steps: 1. Check ordinary ids, empty/null ids, wrong-length ids, wrong-case prefixes, and ids with the prefix not at the start
expected: None is treated as a test id or as stale
notes: Guards against deleting other people's data

scenario: Generated Ids Are Unique
steps: 1. Generate 500 ids within the same time unit
expected: All 500 are distinct

scenario: An Id Stamped In The Future Is Never Treated As Stale
steps:
1. Generate an id stamped in the future
2. Check staleness
expected: Recognised as a test id but never stale (clock skew, or not ours - leave it)

scenario: Purge Deletes Only Stale Test Employees
steps:
1. Fake store holds a stale test employee, a fresh one, someone else's, a look-alike name containing QAR, and one with no id
2. Run the purge
expected: Only the stale test employee is deleted; everything else survives
notes: Mutation-checked: trusting the server's substring match makes this fail

scenario: Purge Refuses To Delete Anything When There Are Suspiciously Many Matches
steps:
1. Fake store holds more stale test employees than the safety cap
2. Run the purge
expected: Nothing is deleted and the refusal is reported
notes: Mutation-checked: removing the cap makes this fail

scenario: Cleanup Deletes Only What This Test Created
steps:
1. Create an employee through TestData; the store also holds another run's marked employee and someone else's
2. Run cleanup
expected: Only this test's employee is deleted

scenario: Cleanup Is Safe When There Is Nothing To Delete, And Safe To Run Twice
steps:
1. Issue an id that is never used and create one employee
2. Run cleanup twice
expected: First run deletes one; second deletes none; nothing throws
notes: Covers a test that fails before saving, and a test that already deleted its own data

scenario: A Failing Cleanup Never Throws, And Reports What It Could Not Remove
steps:
1. Create an employee and make every delete fail
2. Run cleanup
expected: Cleanup retries, does not throw, and reports the employee as leaked for the next purge

scenario: Add User Shows Required Field Errors When Form Is Blank
steps:
1. Log in
2. Go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Confirm no field shows a validation message yet
4. Leave every field empty and click Save
5. Check each field's message
6. Check the page is still the Add User form and no success toast appeared
expected: User Role, Employee Name, Status, Username and Password each show "Required"; Confirm Password shows "Passwords do not match" (verified live - not "Required"). The page stays on the Add User form and no success toast appears (nothing was saved).
notes: Creates no data, so nothing to clean up (a manual probe also saw no create request; the test itself checks the URL and toast, not network traffic). Verified live before automating; the plan's assumption that Confirm Password says "Required" was wrong. One poll-based assertion over a field -> message object, so a failure names the field. The Confirm Password wording looks odd for an empty field (possible app quirk) - asserted as observed; if the app changes it the test fails on purpose for a person to decide.

scenario: Password And Confirm Password Mismatch Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create an employee through the API (the form needs a real one)
2. Log in, go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly, but make Confirm Password differ from Password
4. Check only Confirm Password shows a message
5. Click Save
6. Check the page is still the form, the message remains, and no success toast appeared
7. Search the User Management list for the username
input: Self-created employee; generated username; Password = a generated password, Confirm Password = the same value with an extra character
expected: Confirm Password shows "Passwords do not match" and no other field shows an error. Save does not go through: the page stays on the Add User form with no success toast. Searching the list for that username returns "No Records Found" (no user was created).
notes: Verified live before automating: the message appears as soon as the value is typed (not only on Save), is case-sensitive (a case-only difference still mismatches), and clears when the two match again; Save sent no create request. The employee is created through the API and deleted by teardown (which would also remove a wrongly created user). The test asserts only the extra-character mismatch; case-sensitivity was observed, not tested. Password minimum length and other password rules were NOT verified here (out of scope for this case).

scenario: Username Shorter Than Minimum Length Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create an employee through the API (the form needs a real one)
2. Log in, go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly, but use a 4-character username
4. Check only Username shows a message
5. Click Save
6. Check the page is still the form, the message remains, and no success toast appeared
7. Change the username to 5 characters and check no field shows an error
8. Search the User Management list for the 4-character username
input: Self-created employee; a 4-character username and then a 5-character one, both cut from a generated random value (different every run)
expected: With a 4-character username, only Username shows "Should be at least 5 characters". Save does not go through: the page stays on the Add User form with no success toast. A 5-character username clears the message and the form has no errors (the minimum is exactly 5). Searching the list for the 4-character username returns "No Records Found".
notes: Verified live before automating: lengths 1-4 show the message, 5 and 6 and 40 are accepted, 41 shows "Should not exceed 40 characters" (the maximum is NOT tested here); the message appears as soon as the value is typed, not only on Save; Save sent no create request. The employee is created through the API and deleted by teardown (which would also remove a wrongly created user). The 5-character step presses Tab after typing: one run in ten showed the old message staying on screen for a minute without it. The no-user list check can pass while a create request is still in flight if nothing sits between Save and the search; in this test other steps sit between, and the Username message assertion before Save is the main guard.

scenario: Duplicate Username Is Rejected
steps:
1. Create two employees through the API
2. Create a user for the first employee through the API
3. Log in, go to Admin > User Management and click Add
4. Fill every field validly for the SECOND employee, but reuse the first user's username
5. Check only Username shows a message
6. Click Save
7. Check the page is still the form, the message remains, and no success toast appeared
8. Search the User Management list for that username
input: Two self-created employees; one generated username (used for the first user, then typed again for the second); one generated valid password
expected: Username shows "Already exists" and no other field shows an error. Save does not go through: the page stays on the Add User form with no success toast. Searching the list for that username shows exactly one record, ESS / Enabled, belonging to the FIRST employee.
notes: Verified live before automating: the message "Already exists" appears as soon as the username is typed (the app asks the server; Save is not needed), the check is case-insensitive (the upper-case form is also taken - observed, not tested), a different username clears it, and Save sent no create request. The first user is created through the API (new OrangeHrmApi.createEssUser / TestData.createUser, using the exact request the form sends, ESS and Enabled only); both employees are deleted by teardown, which removes the user too (verified for an API-created user). The not-created check is the exactly-one-record list result, which can pass while a create is still in flight if nothing sits between Save and the search; the Username message assertion before Save is the main guard.

scenario: Cancel Add User Returns To User List
steps:
1. Create an employee through the API (the form needs a real one)
2. Log in, go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly (ESS, Enabled) but do not save
4. Click Cancel
5. Check the page is the User Management list, not the form
6. Search the list for the username
7. Click Add again and check the form is blank
input: Self-created employee; a generated username and a generated valid password, typed into the form and then abandoned
expected: Cancel returns to /admin/viewSystemUsers: the list's Add button is shown and the form's Save button is gone. Searching for the username returns "No Records Found" (the cancelled user was not created). Reopening the Add User form shows empty Username, Password and Confirm Password.
notes: Verified live before automating: Cancel goes straight to the list with no confirmation dialog even when data is typed in, sends no create request, and a reopened form starts blank. The form is filled COMPLETELY so that "no user created" means something - a half-empty form could never be saved anyway. The employee is created through the API and deleted by teardown. The user count on the list is deliberately not checked: the demo is shared and it changes whenever anyone adds a user. Note the "back on the list" check alone would also pass if Save were clicked (Save also lands on the list); the no-user check is what separates them.

scenario: Create User With Minimum-Length 5-Character Username
steps:
1. Create an employee through the API (the form needs a real one)
2. Log in, go to Admin > User Management and click Add
3. Fill every field validly with a 5-character username (ESS, Enabled)
4. Click Save
5. Check the success toast
6. Search the User Management list for the username and check the row
input: Self-created employee; a 5-character username cut from a generated random value (different every run); a generated valid password used for both password fields
expected: The user is saved: the toast "Successfully Saved" appears and the list shows exactly one row for that username with User Role ESS, the employee's name, and Status Enabled.
notes: Added after TC_UCF_005, which proves 4 characters is rejected and 5 clears the message but never saves the 5 - this saves it, so the minimum rests on a real save. Numbered after the planned TC_UCF_006/007 so the plan is not renumbered. Verified live before automating: the save sends the real create request, and deleting the employee afterwards removes this user too (the list then reports "No Records Found" for it). The employee is created through the API and deleted by teardown.

scenario: Search Users By Username Shows The Matching User And Reset Restores The List
steps:
1. Create an employee and a user for it through the API
2. Log in, go to Admin > User Management
3. Enter the username in the search box and click Search
4. Check exactly one record is shown, with the user's role, employee name and status
5. Click Reset
6. Check the search box is empty and the list is no longer filtered
input: Self-created employee and ESS / Enabled user (generated username)
expected: Search shows "(1) Record Found" with that user's row (ESS, the employee's name, Enabled). Reset empties the search box and the list shows more than one record again.
notes: The employee and user are created through the API (TestData.createEmployee / createUser) and the employee is deleted by teardown, which removes the user. Verified live before automating: Search gives "(1) Record Found" with that single row; Reset empties the search box and brings the full list back. The total is NOT asserted - it was 33 users one day and 27 another because the demo is shared - only that it is two or more. The page text has a leading space (" (33) Records Found"), so the regex allows for it (a string match trims it, a regex does not). The Reset check cannot pass early: right after a search the text still says "(1) Record Found" and the assertion waits until it does not.
